data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 names a relation (reduction/abstraction to SRC_003) and a refuter (n independent sub-checks within one record making it n>1), but it never states what the abstraction is REFUTED IF the reduction's core premise holds — it only refutes the downstream single-data-point critique. The covering principle for a reduction relation is that the reduced-to problem class must be closed under the reduction: it fails if 084384ac0b1e exhibits structure (e.g., trace-internal variance across sub-checks) that SRC_003's problem class cannot absorb. SRC_001 gestures at this via 'one record many samples' but stops at the empirical counterexample without naming the principle under which the reduction is invalid. A substantive relation requires the kind-of-relation AND its falsification condition to be stated at the abstraction level, not merely a concrete disproof of a consequence.
